styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Baščaršija bazaar, mosques and Sebilj fountain, with evenings in the old town cafés.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Latin Bridge, the Tunnel of Hope and Yugoslav-era sites on a walk through the 1990s war story.

styles.label: Cuisine
styles.blurb: Ćevapi, burek, baklava and Bosnian coffee, eaten slowly in the old quarter.

stays.why: Walk to the bazaar, Sebilj and most old-town sights. Quiet at night, and narrow streets mean you walk rather than drive.
Near the main boulevard and the river bike lanes. Trams 1, 3 and 4 serve the centre, so reaching the old town is easy.
Central and walkable, with many cafés and shops. Good base for trams and the Nextbike stations along the tram lines.
Quiet residential old-town edge below the fortress. Lovely views, but steep streets and no driving, so pack light.

food: Try ćevapi (grilled minced meat rolls) in Baščaršija, usually served with raw onion and somun bread.
Order burek or sirnica (pastry with meat or cheese) for breakfast, then finish with baklava and Bosnian coffee in a copper pot.
Eat at the bazaar cafés and kebab grills around Baščaršija. Prices are in KM, so check the menu before ordering.
Sit in a traditional kafana for slow coffee and local dishes. Book ahead on weekends if you can.
Pay in KM. Carry some small notes and coins for kiosks and buses, since bus tickets are bought from the driver.
more_time: Take a day trip to Mostar for the old bridge and the old town. Check bus times on the day.
Ride Tram 3 to Ilidža for the spa park and gardens, at the far end of the full line.
Go up Trebević or Jahorina for views over the city and the mountains. Check the transport and weather on the day.

recommend.why: Two nights give you a full day in the old town, a tram ride out to Ilidža and time for a Mostar day trip.

month_notes: Very cold, with highs near 5°C and lows around -4°C. Expect 15 rainy days. Dress in layers and plan indoor sights.
Still cold, with highs near 9°C and lows around -1°C. Fewer rainy days (about 11).
Cool spring weather, with highs near 11°C and lows around 1°C. Pack a warm jacket and an umbrella.
Mild, with highs near 16°C and lows around 4°C. Good for walking the old town and cycling.
Warm and changeable, with highs near 20°C and lows around 9°C. 16 rainy days, so keep an umbrella handy.
Pleasant, with highs near 24°C and lows around 14°C. Good time for river cycling and outdoor cafés.
Hottest month, with highs near 27°C and lows around 16°C. Start walks early and carry water.
Hot, with highs near 27°C and lows around 16°C. Only 10 rainy days, so it is a good month for trips.
Warm, with highs near 22°C and lows around 12°C. Long, clear days for cycling and the mountains.
Mild and dry, with highs near 18°C and lows around 7°C. Good for walking and the autumn colours.
Cool, with highs near 12°C and lows around 3°C. Pack layers for evenings.
Cold, with highs near 8°C and lows around 0°C. Dress warmly and plan indoor sights for some afternoons.

climate_guide.summary: Continental climate with cold, snowy winters and warm, fairly dry summers. Rain is spread through the year.

items.title: Best time: May to June and September
items.text: Highs around 20–24°C with mild nights. Ideal for walking, cycling and the mountains.

items.title: Cold winters (December to February)
items.text: Highs near 5–9°C and lows below freezing. Wear warm layers and waterproof shoes for icy streets.

items.title: Hot summers (July and August)
items.text: Highs around 27°C. Walk early or late in the day and carry water.

items.title: Rain year-round
items.text: Between 9 and 16 rainy days a month. Carry a compact umbrella in every season.

items.title: Mountain weather changes fast
items.text: Higher ground is cooler than the city centre. Check the forecast before any hike or ride.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Warm layers, a waterproof jacket, comfortable walking shoes and a small umbrella. Pack light clothing for summer days.

transit.best: Trams for the centre and Ilidža, walking the old town, and taxis with a meter for late trips.

modes.text: There is no metro in Sarajevo. Use trams and trolleybuses instead.

Trams and trolleybuses run the city. Tram 3 runs the full line from Ilidža to the centre. Tram 1 and 4 serve the central loop. A single ticket costs 2.20 KM and a day ticket costs 7.10 KM. Buy in the Javni prevoz KS app, from drivers or at GRAS kiosks.
Buses cover routes beyond the trams. Buy tickets from the driver for 2.20 KM. Pre-bought tram tickets are not valid on buses.

Legitimate taxis have a TAXI sign and plates with TA. Insist on the meter and ask for a receipt. Official firms include Paja 1522, Žuti 033 66 35 55 and Samir & Emir 1516. Taxis are the main scam risk, so avoid unmarked cars.
Driving is not recommended in the Old Town, where streets are steep, narrow and one-way. Parking is very hard to find. A car is only useful for trips outside the city.
Walking is the best way to see the centre. Street signs are scarce, so use a map app.
Nextbike has about 14 stations along the tram lines. You get 30 free minutes per day, then 1.50 KM after that. Separate bike lanes run along the river and main boulevard for over 5 km.
No ferry service operates in the city.
